summary: Stock reservation and its history commit together through one shared store; concurrent requests cannot oversell or create ordinary partial writes.
Inventory reads and inserted objects are detached; duplicate IDs, cancelled writes, quantity overflow and missing-work-order reservations are rejected.
Inventory routes require the existing Operations policy; part Location links are readable and reservation history is exposed.
Development web proxy now matches the API launch profile on port 5110.
Nine detailed source-grounded learning documents explain ownership, transactions, contracts, failure tests, debugging, exercises and a request trace.

checks.environment: .NET SDK 10.0.302; locked restore; isolated copy; ASP.NET test host and existing SQLite in-memory adapter tests

additional.webBuild: TypeScript and Vite production build passed

limits: Inventory remains in memory with one-process consistency and no durable transaction or retry idempotency key.
Demo headers are not production identity; parts have no campus ownership field.
Work-order existence is checked, but terminal-status policy and cross-module state-transition coordination remain exercises.
The React console displays work orders; inventory UI is a documented capstone.
No live browser, deployed service, inventory database migration or manual HTTP trace was executed.
